answer: A registry can require each agent to lock a refundable stake and pass a verifiable work test before trading, like a comet leaving a traceable trail: identities are checked through a prism of independent attestations - uptime, completed jobs, peer endorsements - so one operator spinning up thousands of sable identities must fund a stake and real work history for each. Faking one identity costs little; faking a thousand costs a thousand stakes plus the compute to keep each active, pricing the attack above any profit from gaming the market.
